definition: Illustrative input-output pairs included in a prompt to demonstrate the desired task and format to a language model.
details: Well-chosen few-shot examples can substantially improve output quality and consistency by clarifying ambiguous instructions through demonstration rather than description alone.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. Boil it down and it is this: Illustrative input-output pairs included in a prompt to demonstrate the desired task and format to a language model. Here is why it matters: Well-chosen few-shot examples can substantially improve output quality and consistency by clarifying ambiguous instructions through demonstration rather than description alone. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Few-Shot Examples.
